newsitem.title: USA: L.A. County mulls $12.6 bln budget, vote expected.
newsitem.headline: L.A. County mulls $12.6 bln budget, vote expected.

text.p: Los Angeles County supervisors will debate the county's proposed $12.6 billion fiscal year 1997-1998 budget on Tuesday, and could take a final vote on the spending plan at the end of the day.

The final budget is slightly larger that the nearly $12 billion plan proposed in April by Los Angeles County's chief administrative officer. The revised 1997-1998 budget would expand the county's workforce by 329 positions.
The budget proposal funds an operating reserve of $29.7 million, but does not include pay raises for county workers.
Most county employees have not had a raise for three years, and for many groups it has been four and five years.
County spokeswoman Judy Hammond said the Board of Supervisors was likely to vote on the budget at the end of Tuesday's session.
The final $12.6 billion budget plan includes a $9.9 billion general fund, up from $9.4 billion proposed in April.
